The geopolitical uncertainties which persisted in the first quarter of the current financial year 
have continued to mar the global economy in Q2, following the reescalation of conflict in West 
Asia, which has driven energy prices sharply higher leading to inflationary concerns and 
increased volatility across financial markets. However, despite these persistent geopolitical 
challenges, the Indian economy has posted a robust growth of 7.8% during Q1, driven by 
domestic consumption and investment. This resilient performance has led to a sharp upward 
revision of India's GDP growth forecast for 2026-27 by IMF to 7% from 6.4% earlier. 
 
This resilience in the domestic economy is also reflected in the Bank's business momentum with 
the Bank's total business growing by 19.4% Y-o-Y to INR3.10 lakhs crores as on 30th September 
2026. The Y-o-Y growth across both deposits and advances has been healthy at 16.3% and 
23.7%, respectively. The profitability has also improved after a subdued performance in the first 
quarter, with the net profit for the quarter being recorded at INR546 crores, a sequential jump of 
almost 29% and a double-digit Y-o-Y growth as well.

On the credit side, in alignment with the Bank's strategic positioning as a retail-focused bank, as 
emphasized during the Q1 call, the Bank has recorded a sequential growth of 7.62% in 
Agricultural Advances and 3.90% in Retail Advances, underscoring the tangible progress made 
in execution. The entire net incremental growth during the quarter has been contributed by 
Retail, Agriculture and MSME loans, that is RAM. And this growth has been contributed by 
both Jammu, Kashmir, Ladakh and Rest of India in almost equal proportions to their share in 
the Bank's outstanding RAM loans. On a YTD basis, more than 60% of the Bank's net 
incremental credit has been contributed by RAM portfolio. 
Within RAM, Bank has registered a Y-o-Y growth of around 17% in Agricultural Advances, 
with a double-digit YTD growth for the first half year. Auto loans continue to be the best-
performing segment amongst retail loans with a Y-o-Y growth of over 25%, doing well both in 
Jammu, Kashmir, Ladakh as well as Rest of India. Housing loans in Rest of India division also 
continued to grow at a healthy pace, recording a double-digit Y-o-Y growth. 
 
On the deposit front also, the bank has already achieved a YTD growth of around 7% against 
our guidance of 10% for the financial year with the growth in Term Deposits continuing to 
outpace the growth in CASA in line with the continuing industry trend. However, the gap 
between the growth in Term Deposits and CASA Deposits has narrowed down in this quarter as 
the bank has been able to record positive CASA inflows during this quarter, after a sharp outflow 
in Q1. As a result, Bank has been able to broadly maintain its CASA ratio at the same level of 
around 42%, being recorded at 41.97% as on 30th September 2026. 
 
Now, coming to profitability, the Bank has recorded an operating profit of INR789 crores for 
the quarter, registering a 27% Y-o-Y growth and a 12% Q-o-Q growth. Even on a half year basis, 
the Bank has recorded a Y-o-Y growth of over 15% in Operating Profit, being recorded at 
INR1,492 crores for the first half year of the current fiscal. While the operating income for this 
quarter has grown by over 6% sequentially and 14.5% Y-o-Y, the increase in operating 
expenditure continues to be controlled at just 2% Q-o-Q and 6.5% Y-o-Y, contributing towards 
improved profitability for the quarter. As a result, Cost-to-Income Ratio of the Bank for this 
quarter has also moderated substantially on both sequential and Y-o-Y basis, being recorded at 
56.57% for the quarter. 
 
Yield on advances has remained broadly flat on a sequential basis, being recorded at 8.55% for 
the quarter. However, the increasing contribution of RAM segment to our incremental credit 
portfolio, coupled with the recent repo rate hike, is expected to support an improvement in the 
yield from the third quarter onwards. The sharp outflow of CASA deposits during Q1 continued 
to weigh on our liability profile, contributing to an increase in the Cost of Deposits in this quarter 
to 4.85%. However, with the surplus liquidity in the banking system easing bulk deposit rates 
combined with the positive CASA inflows in Q2 and the reduction in Term Deposit rates by our 
Bank in this quarter, we expect moderation in the Cost of Deposits going forward. Resultantly, 
the NIM has witnessed compression, being recorded at 3.22% for the half year but with the 
expected improvement across both yield and cost, the NIM should also improve.

Notwithstanding the prevailing macro-economic uncertainties, the Bank has witnessed a notable 
moderation in slippages during the current fiscal, with Annualized Gross Slippage Ratio of just 
0.4% for the half year, as Gross Slippages, in terms of absolute amount, have halved compared 
to the corresponding period last year. This reflects the resilience of our portfolio and the 
continued effectiveness of our underwriting and monitoring mechanisms. The asset quality 
metrics also continue to consistently improve reaching decadal best numbers with GNPA and 
NNPA as on 30-09-2026 being recorded at 2.23% and 0.51% respectively and PCR improving 
from 90.53% as on 30th June 2026 to 91.76% as on 30th September 2026. 
 
Capital Adequacy Ratio has been recorded at 16.57% as on 30th September 2026 with CET 1 of 
13.88%. The Bank is already in the process of raising both equity and debt capital to the tune of 
INR1,000 crores and INR500 crores respectively and will raise the capital at an opportune time 
to support its future growth. 
 
On the back of improved profitability, RoA has jumped by 20 bps Q-o-Q, while RoE has jumped 
by more than 250 bps Q-o-Q and have been recorded at 1.07% and 13.68% respectively for the 
quarter. 
 
Based on the mid-term review, we have reassessed our guidance as indicated in the last call. The 
revised guidance for FY 2026-27 would be credit growth of 14% plus, deposit growth of 12% 
plus, CASA to be 42% plus. There should be a considerable improvement in NIM, ROA to be 
around 1.20% and GNPA to be below 2%.

questions now.
